div.head: III Eg 8.3
div.ab: ⁊ gif hwa hi þonne undeoror sille, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gilde ægðer þam cynge XL scill' ge se þe hi sille ge se þe hi bicge.
⁊ gyf hwa hy þonne undeoror sylle, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gylde ægþer þam cynge LX scill' ge se ðe hy sylle ge se þe hy bicge.
[Not in G(A), Ld.] ⁊ gyf hwa hi þonne undeoror sylle, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gylde ægþer þam cynge LX seyllinga ge se þe hy sylle ge se ðe hy bicge. [A]
⁊ gyf hwa hi þonne undeoror sylle, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gylde ægþer þam cynge LX scyllinga ge se þe hy sylle ge se ðe hy bicge.
⁊ gif hwa hi þonne undeoror sille, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gilde ægðer þam cynge LX scill' ge se þe hi sille ge se þe hi bicge.
And gyf hwa hi þonne undeoror sylle, oððe eawunga oððe dearnunga, gylde ægþer þam cynge LX scyllinga ge se þe hy sylle ge se þe hy bicge.
(Und wenn sie jemand nun billiger verkauft, entweder öffentlich oder heimlich, so zahle sowohl wer sie verkauft, als wer sie kauft dem König 60 (40 D) Schill. A D G2.)
(And if anyone sells it more cheaply, either openly or secretly, let both the seller and the buyer pay the king 60 (40, D) shillings. A D G2.)
And if anyone sells it at a cheaper rate, either openly or secretly, both he who sells it and he who buys it shall pay 60 shillings to the king.
[And if anyone sells it cheaper, whether openly or secretly, both he who sells and he who buys are to pay 60 shillings to the king.]
And if anyone does sell it at a lower price, either publicly or in secret, both the seller and the buyer are to pay the king sixty shillings.
div.note: Not in G or Ld; K gives A's text. D reads XL, to be corrected to LX from A and G2. In A, a charter of Oswald of York (c. 972) follows in another hand, then I–II Cn; in D and G2, V Atr follows in the same hand.

Der Satz steht nur in zweiter Rezension
The sentence occurs only in the second recension

Da nur D, gegen AG 2, 40 liest, ist dies sein Fehler. Die beiden Händler zusammen zahlen also Königs ‘Ungehorsam’ (s. d. Gl 14), wie für andere Verletzungen der gesetzlichen Schranken des Handels (s. d. Gl 8b); I Ew 1, 1

Since only D, against AG 2, reads 40, this is its error. The two traders together thus pay the king’s ‘disobedience’ (see that word in Gl 14), as for other breaches of the legal restrictions on trade (see that word in Gl 8b); I Ew 1, 1
This clause is found only in the second recension.
D’s reading xl scill. as against lx scill. in A, G₂ is probably a scribal error. Liebermann points out that seller and buyer together pay the regular fine of 120 shillings to the king.
